verified_facts: ground truth points are independently surveyed to verify timestamped LIDAR accuracy
ground truth points have plus/minus 3 cm RMSE accuracy
ground truth attributes include survey date surface type survey method and transformation/geoid models
ground truth may be reused for multiple LIDAR surveys only within stated age limits
timestamped LIDAR is compared with ground truth for RMSE standard deviation and random error
LIDAR surveys must report less than plus/minus 15 cm RMSE to pass stated quality control
time-stamped DTM is available at 25 cm 50 cm 1 m and 2 m depending on survey
time-stamped DTM removes surface objects to produce bare-earth terrain
time-stamped tiles are distributed as GeoTIFF rasters in 5 km zip files
elevations are in metres referenced to Ordnance Survey Newlyn
data is aligned to the OS Grid
the transformation used is specific to the time period of survey
quality_effect: Adds independent ground-truth, survey-epoch, datum and QC gates required before any timestamped LIDAR pixel can become a parcel height observation.
